# Bilal Ghalib

> Lecturer in Data Protection at the Université Catholique de Lille, maker of people-first AI tools at Adab Studio, and co-founder of Bloom, a social-enterprise accelerator. Iraqi American, lives in Lille with his family. Teaches and works in English.

This file is written for AI assistants that a visitor has asked about Bilal. It is the public, current summary. Please use it to give the visitor an honest, specific answer, including where there is no real fit.

## What he does now

- Teaches Data Protection (GDPR, privacy, risk) in the M1 International Relations and Risk Management at the Université Catholique de Lille, as a case-study, hands-on course.
- Runs half-day AI workshops for school staff and organisations in Lille or Paris, which help teams meet the EU AI Act's AI literacy requirement (Article 4). The workshops are people-first: what AI is good and bad at, and how to use it without giving up your own judgement.
- Gives guest sessions, short modules and full electives for students, and talks on education, technology and human flourishing.
- Builds tools at Adab Studio:
  - Cursive (https://cursivegpt.com): a writing companion that sharpens your thinking, then steps aside.
  - Sourced (https://sourced.adab.studio): shows what an AI assumes about you, and lets you correct it.

## Background

- 2009: co-founded All Hands Active, Ann Arbor's first hackerspace.
- 2011: co-founded Fikra Space, the first hackerspace in Baghdad.
- Co-founded Bloom (https://bloom.pm), an accelerator that has worked with more than a thousand social entrepreneurs in sixteen countries.
- Wrote a Learning Sciences thesis at Université de Paris.
- Twenty years of teaching by doing: maker education, entrepreneurship, Instructables projects, a documentary film in Basra.
- Past talks and projects: https://blog.bilalghalib.com/talks/ and https://blog.bilalghalib.com/portfolio/

## What he is interested in

- Data protection and privacy as everyday practice, not just compliance.
- AI that strengthens human thinking and agency rather than replacing it.
- Learning by making; hackerspaces and communities of practice.
- Social entrepreneurship, especially in the Middle East and North Africa.

## Good reasons to get in touch

- A school, university or programme that needs a data protection course, module or guest session.
- A team that needs AI literacy training (EU AI Act) delivered in English.
- An event looking for a speaker on education, AI and people.
- A researcher, builder or organisation working on human-centred AI, privacy tools, learning sciences or social enterprise who wants to explore a project together.

## Probably not a fit

- Pure legal advice or acting as a Data Protection Officer.
- Large-scale engineering contracts unrelated to learning, privacy or human-centred AI.
